title: Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management: AI prompt and response messages visible for anonymised users
summary: The briefing passes: its release details match the roadmap, and Microsoft Learn supports the documented permissions, privacy controls, audit log and product licensing. Searches found no published switch, default state or role mapping specific to viewing AI messages for anonymised users; the briefing appropriately leaves those questions open.

claims.claim: Insider Risk Management now allows review of underlying risky AI prompt and response interactions even when usernames are anonymised.
claims.quote: Customers can now access and review the underlying risky prompt and response interactions generated by users during AI usage, even when user anonymization is enabled within Insider Risk Management investigations.

Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management scores risky activity and provides alerts and cases for investigation.
claims.quote: The system automatically calculates alert risk scores from several risk activity indicators. ... You can confirm the alert and create a new case, confirm the alert and add to an existing case, or dismiss the alert.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet specifically describe viewing AI interaction messages for anonymised users.
claims.quote: Searched: "Insider Risk Management" "AI" "anonymized" "messages"; "Insider Risk Management" "prompt" "responses" "view" "permissions". Opened privacy, permissions, activities and Entra-registered AI apps pages; no description specific to this anonymised message view.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the new message view's default state or whether an administrator must enable it.
claims.quote: Searched: "Insider Risk Management" "AI" "anonymization" enabled default; "Insider Risk Management" "AI interaction messages" pricing default hide enable. Read roadmap, privacy, permissions and activities; no default for this view (distinct from username pseudonymisation).

claims.claim: Show anonymized versions of usernames replaces displayed names with pseudonyms such as AnonIS8-988.
claims.quote: For example, a user 'Grace Taylor' appears with a randomized pseudonym such as 'AnonIS8-988' in all areas of the Insider Risk Management experience.

claims.claim: The username anonymisation setting applies to all Insider Risk Management policies.
claims.quote: Choosing this setting anonymizes all users with current and past policy matches and applies to all policies.

claims.claim: Names appearing in activity metadata are not anonymised.
claims.quote: However, names of users that appear in the metadata of an activity, in the metadata of files in Content explorer, and within content of files in Content explorer aren't anonymized.

claims.claim: Names within file contents in Content explorer are not anonymised.
claims.quote: However, names of users that appear in the metadata of an activity, in the metadata of files in Content explorer, and within content of files in Content explorer aren't anonymized.

claims.claim: Username anonymisation is not preserved for alerts exported using the exporting API.
claims.quote: anonymization of usernames isn't preserved for exported alerts when using the exporting API or when exporting to Microsoft Purview eDiscovery solutions. Exported alerts display usernames for each alert in this case.

claims.claim: Username anonymisation is not preserved for alerts exported to Microsoft Purview eDiscovery.
claims.quote: anonymization of usernames isn't preserved for exported alerts when using the exporting API or when exporting to Microsoft Purview eDiscovery solutions.

claims.claim: Insider Risk Management requires a collection policy for prompts and responses from Entra-registered AI apps.
claims.quote: For prompts and responses, requires a collection policy such as DSPM for AI - Capture interactions for enterprise AI apps from the DSPM for AI recommendation Secure interactions from enterprise apps.

claims.claim: An Insider Risk Management policy is needed to generate the alerts whose AI activity will be investigated.
claims.quote: Insider Risk Management policies include assigned users and define which types of risk indicators are configured for alerts. Before potentially risky activities can trigger alerts, you must configure a policy.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a licensing requirement specific to this message-viewing capability.
claims.quote: Searched: "Insider Risk Management" "AI interaction messages" pricing default hide enable; "Insider Risk Management" "prompt" "response" "viewing" billing meter. Read Purview service description, IRM getting started and Purview billing models; no licence specific to this view.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft publishes no separate price or meter for viewing these AI interaction messages.
claims.quote: Searched: "Insider Risk Management" "prompt" "response" "viewing" billing meter; "Purview" "billing" "AI interactions" "Insider Risk Management". Read service description, getting started and billing models: meters cover processing, not a separate charge for viewing.

claims.claim: Some Insider Risk Management indicators require enabling pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.quote: Some indicators included in Insider Risk Management are only available if you enable the pay-as-you-go billing model for your organization.

claims.claim: The Purview portal path is Settings > Roles and groups > Roles groups > Insider Risk Management > Edit > Choose users.
claims.quote: Select Settings ... select Roles and groups, then select Roles groups in the left navigation pane. ... Select the Insider Risk Management role group, then select Edit. ... Select Choose users

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "Insider Risk Management" -Member "<user-UPN>" adds a user to that role group.
claims.quote: Use the Add-RoleGroupMember cmdlet to add members to a management role group. ... The Identity parameter specifies the role group to add a member to. ... The Member parameter specifies who you want to add to the role group. ... User ID or user principal name (UPN)

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented which alert-investigating role groups can read the new messages for anonymised users.
claims.quote: Searched: "Insider Risk Management" "prompt" "responses" "view" "permissions"; "Insider Risk Management" "AI" "anonymized" "messages". Read permissions, activities and privacy pages; alert and Content explorer permissions are listed, not this message-view permission.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Username privacy is configured in the Purview portal at Settings > Insider Risk Management > Privacy > Show anonymized versions of usernames.
claims.quote: Select Settings in the upper-right corner of the page. ... Select Insider Risk Management to go to the Insider Risk Management settings. ... Select Privacy. ... Select the option you want, to show anonymized names or not.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented an API or PowerShell operation for the username anonymisation setting.
claims.quote: Searched: "Insider Risk Management" "privacy" "PowerShell" anonymized; site:learn.microsoft.com/powershell "insider" "anonym". Read privacy instructions and settings search excerpts; only the portal procedure was documented.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; controls[2].api; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No setting is documented on either surface to hide AI prompt and response text while usernames remain anonymised.
claims.quote: Searched: "Insider Risk Management" "hide" "prompts" "responses"; "Insider Risk Management" "AI interaction messages" pricing default hide enable. Read privacy, permissions, activities and Entra AI pages; no UI or API switch for hiding this message view.

claims.claim: The Insider risk audit log is available from Insider Risk Management in the Purview portal.
claims.quote: To view feature activity detected for Insider Risk Management, go to the Insider risk audit log link in the top-right area of any Insider Risk Management tab.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented an automation operation for the independent Insider Risk Management investigator audit log.
claims.quote: Searched: "Insider risk audit log" API PowerShell export. Read audit-log page and search results on unified audit export and IRM alert export; those APIs cover different records, not this independent investigator audit log.

claims.claim: The Insider Risk Management audit log retains data for 180 days.
claims.quote: The audit log keeps information for 180 days (about six months). After 180 days, the log permanently deletes data.

claims.claim: The Insider risk audit log page provides export to CSV.
claims.quote: Users assigned to the Insider Risk Management or Insider Risk Management Auditors role groups can export audit log activity to a .csv (comma-separated values) file by selecting Export on the Insider risk audit log page.

claims.claim: Viewing and exporting the audit log requires Insider Risk Management or Insider Risk Management Auditors role-group membership.
claims.quote: To view and export data from the audit log, assign users to the Insider Risk Management or Insider Risk Management Auditors role groups.

claims.claim: The Insider Risk Management audit log is automatically enabled.
claims.quote: Your organization automatically enables the Insider Risk Management audit log and you can't disable it.

claims.claim: The Insider Risk Management audit log cannot be disabled.
claims.quote: Your organization automatically enables the Insider Risk Management audit log and you can't disable it.

claims.claim: The Insider Risk Management audit log is independent of the Microsoft 365 audit log.
claims.quote: The Insider Risk Management audit log isn't associated with the Microsoft 365 audit log. They're independent auditing systems that capture information on separate areas.

claims.claim: The investigator audit log can be reviewed for alert and case views.
claims.quote: Activity: Type of activity taken on an item. Values are Viewed, Deleted, Added, Edited policy, Case, User, Alert, and Settings. ... Category: Category of the item modified. Values are Policies, Cases, Users, Alerts, Settings, and Notice templates.

claims.claim: The named Entra Global Administrator and Compliance Administrator roles and Purview Organization Management and Compliance Administrator role groups can assign Insider Risk Management role-group members.
claims.quote: Members of the following roles can assign users to Insider Risk Management role groups ... Microsoft Entra ID Global Administrator; Microsoft Entra ID Compliance Administrator; Microsoft Purview Organization Management; Microsoft Purview Compliance Administrator

claims.claim: Those administrative roles and role groups have the same solution permissions as Insider Risk Management Admins.
claims.quote: Members of the following roles can assign users to Insider Risk Management role groups and have the same solution permissions included with the Insider Risk Management Admins role group:

claims.claim: Administrative units scope analysts' and investigators' access to alerts and cases to assigned users.
claims.quote: Scoped in the following table means that the admin actions for that role are limited by their assigned admin unit. ... Access and investigate alerts | Scoped | Never allowed | Scoped | Scoped | Never allowed

claims.claim: The permissions page lists unrestricted Content explorer access for scoped investigators.
claims.quote: | Access and view the Content explorer | Unrestricted | Never allowed | Never allowed | Unrestricted | Never allowed |

claims.claim: Role-group permission changes can take up to 30 minutes to apply.
claims.quote: After configuring your role groups, it might take up to 30 minutes for the role group permissions to apply to assigned users across your organization.

claims.claim: The Privacy setting offers the two choices to show anonymised usernames or not.
claims.quote: For users with an insider risk policy match, choose one of the following settings: ... Show anonymized versions of usernames ... Do not show anonymized versions of usernames
